teaser.text: Carrier Global sells the equipment and controls that keep buildings comfortable and temperature-sensitive cargo safe. Its business earns money when those products are made, installed, serviced and monitored over time.

stock.title: Carrier stock forecast
stock.meta_description: Carrier's weighted forecast is lower first, then roughly flat, before rising, hinging on profit, cash generation and debt reduction.
stock.opening: Carrier's weighted forecast is $45.37 in October 2027, rising to $60.94 in October 2029. It hinges on commercial and data-center deliveries converting to profit while residential demand and factory utilization recover.
stock.closing: The full Carrier memo also answers how Carrier's business works, who its rivals are, how management is executing, and what risks could change the cases.

blocks.heading: Where could Carrier's shares be by October 2029?

paragraphs.text: The weighted price is $45.37 in October 2027, a 16% loss from $55.00 including dividends. It rises to $53.11 in October 2028, or roughly flat, and reaches $60.94 in October 2029, a 16% gain. The forecast assigns 30% to the bear case, 50% to the base case and 20% to the bull case.

blocks.heading: What has to go right or wrong for Carrier?

paragraphs.text: The bear case gives $2.64 billion, $2.79 billion and $2.99 billion as commercial conversion falters and residential weakness persists. The bull case gives $3.55 billion, $3.98 billion and $4.42 billion because commercial and data-center deliveries improve utilization and margins. Q2 total orders grew about 40%, while data-center orders grew more than 300%, but orders can be delayed or canceled.

blocks.heading: How much cash does Carrier really make?

paragraphs.text: Free cash flow subtracts capital spending from operating cash flow. Carrier published free cash flow of $2,121 million for 2025. Using continuing operating cash flow and $392 million of continuing capital spending produces about $1,697 million, a better view of the ongoing business.

Shares fall in every case, but at different speeds. The base count moves from 799.6 million to 770.9 million, supported by $1.0 billion annual buybacks and partly offset by compensation issuance. The bear case ends at 802.3 million because buybacks fall to $0.3 billion by the third year. The bull case reaches 764.3 million on $1.5 billion annual buybacks. Carrier had 824.325 million shares outstanding in July and repurchased 12.0 million in the first half, supporting continued reductions.

blocks.heading: What does an investor pay for Carrier today?

paragraphs.text: The price-to-earnings ratio shows what investors pay for each dollar of annual profit. The next-twelve-month P/E implies about $3.29 of earnings per share. That is above Carrier’s latest 2026 adjusted EPS guidance of $2.90, so the apparently moderate valuation already depends on improvement beyond the current outlook.

blocks.heading: How much does Carrier pay per share over time?

paragraphs.text: Free cash flow is operating cash after capital spending. It can fund dividends, debt repayment, buybacks or acquisitions, so it is not automatically cash for shareholders. In the first half of 2026, Carrier generated $795 million of free cash flow. It paid $400 million in common dividends.

blocks.heading: Where does Carrier’s free cash flow go?

paragraphs.subsection: 3.5 — Divestiture proceeds, debt and shareholder returns
paragraphs.text: Investment also matters. Carrier’s research and development spending was $625 million in 2025, down from $686 million in 2024. In the first half of 2026, free cash flow was $795 million, while buybacks and dividends together exceeded it. That can be sensible after asset sales, but it cannot continue indefinitely without more borrowing or less investment.

paragraphs.text: The base dividend rises from $1.00 to $1.08 per share. The bear case holds it at $0.96, the current annualized payout, while the bull case reaches $1.28. The base assumes modest increases because Carrier expects to continue quarterly payments, but debt, investment and claims limit the pace.

paragraphs.subsection: 3.5 — Divestiture proceeds, debt and shareholder returns
paragraphs.text: Carrier says its priorities are organic investment, acquisitions, a growing dividend and then repurchases. The final judgment should therefore rest on whether Viessmann produces durable organic growth, stronger margins and returns above its cost of capital. Until then, Carrier has made a coherent strategic shift, but not yet a fully demonstrated financial success.

earnings.title: Carrier earnings date and guidance
earnings.meta_description: Carrier reports October 29, 2026; guidance calls for $23 billion sales, $2.90 adjusted EPS and $2 billion free cash flow.
earnings.opening: Carrier's next results are due on October 29, 2026. Watch whether commercial equipment shipped as planned.
earnings.closing: The full Carrier memo also explains its business, rivals, management and risks.

paragraphs.text: On July 28, Carrier raised its sales target for the year ending December 2026 to approximately $23 billion and its adjusted earnings-per-share target to approximately $2.90. Adjusted earnings per share means profit per share after removing selected items that management considers separate from underlying operations. The increase followed a better first half and a return to organic sales growth, which excludes currency movements and acquisitions or disposals.

Commercial cooling is the harder test. Carrier expects second-half adjusted operating profit and EPS to grow approximately 50% from a year earlier. It also expects $1.5 billion of second-half data-center sales, supporting approximately $2 billion for the full year. A backlog is a queue of orders, not revenue or cash: Carrier must still obtain parts, build the equipment, test it and deliver it. Management calls the second half fully booked, so execution at the factories now matters as much as demand.

blocks.heading: Did Carrier keep its past promises?

paragraphs.text: The 2025 annual bonus shows firmer discipline. Carrier missed its sales, adjusted operating-profit and free-cash-flow targets. The company performance factor fell to 39%, and the committee added no individual uplift. Gitlin’s bonus was US$1,023,750 and Goris’s was US$351,000. A weak year therefore reduced their bonuses without eliminating their longer-term awards.

blocks.heading: What has Carrier's last eight quarters shown about sales and profit?

paragraphs.text: Organic sales growth removes specified effects such as acquisitions, divestitures and currency. It still combines price, the number of machines sold and the mix of products. Organic growth was 4% in Q3 2024, then became a 9% decline in Q4 2025. It returned to 3% growth in Q2 2026, but that recovery does not by itself prove that Carrier sold more units.

Carrier exceeded EPS estimates in six of the eight quarters from the third quarter of 2024 through the second quarter of 2026. It missed in two. The latest miss came in the fourth quarter of 2025, while both first two quarters of 2026 beat expectations. That record is encouraging but too short to make another beat automatic.
